Corollary
[Gauss's Theorema Egregium]

Source: petersen:page-0112 ↗ thm:pet-ch3-tangential-curvature-equation ↗ ex:pet-ch3-euclidean-flat

When $M^3=\mathbb R^3$ (so $R\equiv 0$) and $E_1,E_2$ is an orthonormal basis of $T_pH$ for a surface $H\subset \mathbb R^3$, \[ \sec (T_pH)=R^H(E_1,E_2,E_2,E_1)=\Pi (E_1,E_1)\Pi (E_2,E_2)-\Pi (E_1,E_2)^2=\det [\Pi ], \] i.e. the extrinsic quantity $\det [\Pi ]$ equals the intrinsic sectional curvature $\sec (T_pH)$.
Proof

↗ cor:pet-ch3-gauss-egregium \sketch Apply the Gauss equation to $X=W=E_1$, $Y=Z=E_2$. The ambient curvature vanishes by item 4, and orthonormality identifies the intrinsic curvature term with $\sec (T_pH)$, leaving $\sec (T_pH)=\det [\Pi ]$.

□
